title: FDA Clears AI-Powered Platform for Converting Spine MRIs to 3D Visualizations
key_facts: The FDA has issued a 510(k) clearance for NextMR, an AI-enabled cloud platform from MRI2CT that generates 3D bone images from conventional 1.5T and 3T spine MRI.
MRI2CT says the platform produces 3D bone morphology in less than 60 seconds, with axial, sagittal and coronal views and a 3D reconstruction.
No local software installation is needed; the platform is a secure cloud application.

Frank Phillips, MD, director of minimally invasive spine surgery at Midwest Orthopaedics at Rush in Chicago, calls it a 'huge advantage' and says it can mean avoiding extra imaging, radiation and appointments.
The article gives no clearance date and no study data for accuracy.
quote_evidence: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a 510(k) clearance for NextMR, an AI-enabled platform that generates 3D bone images of spine imaging obtained with conventional 1.5T and 3T MRI.
For patients, that can mean avoiding additional imaging, radiation and appointments while helping streamline their path to surgery.
why_it_matters_hint: An FDA-cleared AI tool could speed surgical planning for spine patients; the speed and accuracy claims come from the developer and a surgeon.
event_date: Not stated in article; reported 7 Oct 2026
notes: The 'reportedly' hedge is kept for the developer's speed figure. Clearance date not given in the article, so freshness is NEW. Frank Phillips, MD is quoted, not a study author.
